_partNote: Class images for the explorer tiles, rendered at about 74px. The trap on this sheet is that CT and MRI are the same object to a generator, so class I is drawn as a square-fronted gantry with a patient table and class II as the bare cylindrical magnet on a plinth with a quench turret and no table at all. Class V is deliberately not a C-arm, because a C-arm is fluoroscopy and fluoroscopy is an entry in class I; it uses a robot cart instead. The rest are chosen for how far apart they read: a small shielded pot beside a vial, a hand-held wedge with a cable, a small flat can with two curling leads, and a thin sealed pouch. Class II was regenerated: both first candidates drew a small blind-bored fitting that read as a pipe part or a camera, and the fix was to say room-sized machine, stand it on two plinths, and ask for the background to show through the bore.
style: Minimalist technical illustration, the style of a precise patent drawing crossed with an isometric product sketch. Uniform-weight dark slate-gray ink linework with sparse, muted steel-blue accent shading (hex 4E7AA8) on a plain very light warm-gray background (hex F2F3F1). Three-quarter isometric view, single centered subject, generous margins. No text, no labels, no callouts, no logos, no humans, no background scenery, no drop shadows. Clean, engineered, calm. Strictly two colors plus the background: dark slate-gray line and muted steel-blue fill. Every material, including titanium, lead, glass, plastic tubing and cable, is drawn in that same palette. Absolutely no copper, brass, bronze, gold, orange, red, yellow or green anywhere, even where the real object would be that color, and nothing that reads as blood, tissue or skin. Favor open, airy linework with large unfilled light areas over heavy solid gray shading; the drawing should read as line art, not as a rendered solid model. Draw the subject as one whole object seen from outside. Do not draw a cutaway, a section view or an exploded assembly.

partPrompts.1: A computed tomography scanner seen three-quarter: an upright square-fronted housing, wide and shallow front to back like a thick slab standing on end, with one large circular opening cut through its center, and a flat narrow patient table on a plain rectangular pedestal standing in front of it with its long axis pointing at the opening. The square face around a big round hole is the identifying geometry. One machine alone, empty table, no patient, no room, no ceiling rails, no control console.
partPrompts.2: A large superconducting magnet seen three-quarter, drawn as a room-sized machine rather than a small part: a massive drum lying on its side with its axis horizontal, as deep front to back as it is tall, standing on two low plinths, with a wide smooth tunnel bored straight through it from front to back so the plain light background is clearly visible through the opening and out the other side. A shallow flared cowling rings the front opening. One short cylindrical turret stands on top of the drum with a straight pipe rising from it. Heavy and architectural, the open tunnel the identifying feature. Not a small fitting and not a lens: no blind hole, no camera body, no threads, no square housing, no patient table, no room.
partPrompts.3: A small thick-walled shielded container standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter, with one small vial standing upright beside it: the container is a squat heavy cylinder with visibly thick walls, a stepped screw-on lid sitting slightly proud of the body, and a plain flat base; the vial is a plain small cylinder about a third its height with a flat crimped cap. Two objects only, close together, the heavy pot clearly dominant. No syringe, no tongs, no bench, no markings, no radiation symbol.
partPrompts.4: A hand-held ultrasound transducer lying on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a smooth molded wedge-shaped grip, rounded and comfortable in outline, narrowing at one end to a broad slightly convex scanning face with a fine straight parting line across it, and a thick flexible cable leaving the opposite end and curving away in one loose arc before running off. Hand-sized, one object plus its cable. No screen, no cart, no gel, no patient, no second probe.
partPrompts.5: A surgical robot instrument arm on a wheeled cart, seen three-quarter: a single vertical column on a low four-castor base, carrying one slender multi-jointed arm that folds through three plain hinge joints and ends pointing downward, with one straight thin instrument shaft held in a simple carriage at its tip. Column plus one folded arm, and nothing else. No patient, no table, no drapes, no surgeon console, no second arm, no C-shaped arc.
partPrompts.6: An implantable pulse generator lying on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a small flat rounded-rectangular metal can, thin in profile with softly radiused corners, a molded clear header block sitting along its top edge with two small round sockets in it, and two thin flexible leads plugged into those sockets curving away across the surface, each ending in a fine open helical coil. Small and flat, the can plus two curling leads the whole silhouette. No chest, no anatomy, no packaging, no programmer, no markings on the can.
partPrompts.7: A sealed sterile barrier pouch lying flat on a plain surface, seen three-quarter from above: a thin flat rectangular pouch with a wide plain sealed border running all the way around, a band of repeating chevron marks pressed into the seal across one short end, one corner of the top layer peeled slightly back and standing up in a soft curl, and a completely blank unmarked face. Flat, thin and papery, one pouch alone. No instrument visible, no printing, no barcode, no tray, no box.
